items.title: South Asian cinema shines at 51st TIFF: Malayalam film Half makes history
items.summary: With less than four weeks remaining until the 51st Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), around 220 titles have been revealed in the line-ups across the Gala, Platform, Midnight Madness, Centrepiece, and Special Presentations sections. Prominently featured among them are works by Indian-Canadian filmmakers such as Richie Mehta’s Phoolan , Ian Bawa’s Strong Son , Dr Roshan Sethi’s The Surgeon , London-based Naga filmmaker Theja Rio’s Angh as well as Tamil director Karthik Subbaraj’s Dorothy . In a major achievement for Malayalam cinema, director Samjad’s action drama Half has been selected for the iconic Midnight Madness section. Furthermore, under the festival’s Classic Cinema section, a newly restored 4K version of the late, legendary director John Abraham’s final masterpiece from 1986, Amma Ariyan (Report to Mother), will also be screened. Phoolan Starring Sneha Kumari as Phoolan Devi, director Richie Mehta’s Phoolan is based on the autobiography I, Phoolan Devi: The Autobiography of India’s Bandit Queen . The ensemble cast includes Anurag Thakur, Vikram Pratap Singh, Aakash Dahiya, Prateek Pachouri, and Devdutt Banodiya. Phoolan Devi’s dramatic transformation from a Chambal dacoit to a Member of the Parliament was a subject of intense debate in India for over two decades. Richie Mehta’s narrative focuses heavily on the pivotal 48-hour standoff involving nearly 2,000 military personnel that ultimately led to her surrender. This is not the first time Phoolan Devi’s story has reached the screen. Shekhar Kapur previously directed the acclaimed 1994 film Bandit Queen , starring Seema Biswas, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film alongside Best Actress for Biswas. Richie Mehta, who is also behind the Emmy Award-winning Netflix series Delhi Crime (Season 1) and Amazon Prime’s Poacher , holds global streaming distribution rights for Phoolan via Prime Video. “During the making of this film, I was granted complete creative freedom to translate my precise artistic vision onto the screen,” Mehta stated. Mehta’s debut feature Amal was selected for the San Francisco International Asian American Film Festival in 2007, earning Rupinder Nagra a Best Actor award at the 2008 Whistler Film Festival. His 2013 feature Siddharth garnered significant international acclaim at the Toronto and Pyongyang film festivals. items.title: Brij Bhushan’s acquittal raises questions over how the court read the evidence
items.summary: On August 3, 2026, a Delhi trial court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, the former Wrestling Federation of India president, of charges under Sections 354, 354A, and 506(I) of the Indian Penal Code in the sexual harassment case brought by six women wrestlers. Vinod Tomar, the WFI’s former assistant secretary, was acquitted of the remaining charge against him. The court held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. That conclusion is not, by itself, unusual. Criminal courts are required to acquit where the prosecution evidence leaves a reasonable doubt. What deserves closer examination is the route this particular judgment took to get there. The case so far The allegations went back to January 2023, when some of India’s most decorated wrestlers, including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia, sat down in protest at Jantar Mantar, accusing Singh of sexually harassing junior wrestlers over several years, at training camps, tournaments, and federation events. Singh, then a six-time BJP MP, denied everything and dared the wrestlers to prove it in court. It took months of protest, and a nudge from the Supreme Court, before Delhi Police registered two separate FIRs against Singh in April 2023 – one under the IPC for the adult complainants, and a second under the POCSO Act for the seventh, minor complainant. The POCSO case never made it to trial: the minor later withdrew her allegations, police filed a cancellation report, and the case was formally closed in May 2025. The IPC case, brought by the six adult complainants, is the one that reached trial. A chargesheet followed in June 2023, and in May 2024 a magistrate ordered charges framed against Singh under Sections 354, 354A, 354D, and 506 IPC. That trial ran for more than two years, held partly in camera, before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar delivered the acquittal on August 3. Two complainants had turned hostile at trial, telling the court they had been “forced” or “pressured” into making the allegations. The judgment leaned heavily on this, concluding that the case looked “false and fabricated, made collectively” in what it called a “deep conspiracy” that seemed “motivated politically.” Singh, for his part, called the verdict a vindication and said the judiciary had used the word “honour” while acquitting him. items.title: BJP leader Nainar Nagendran targets Vijay’s mother, faces backlash
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nainar Nagendran has sparked a political controversy after making a personal remark involving Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief C Joseph Vijay’s mother. Speaking at the launch of Oru Naadu 2.0 in Chennai on Saturday, August 15, Nagendran said, “In the legislative assembly, some are searching for a father. But only by asking the mother at home can one know who the father is.” He added, “Who will reveal if he is being searched for in the Assembly? This is the situation of the present government.” Nagendran’s remarks were in response to an earlier comment by Vijay in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. Vijay had, on June 23, narrated a story about an elderly man looking for a child’s father and asking, “Where’s your father? I can’t find him.” The remark was understood as a veiled reference to former Chief Minister MK Stalin, who had lost his Assembly seat in the 2026 election. Nagendran appeared to turn Vijay’s “father” reference back on him. He said, “If he wants to know who the father is, he should go ask his mother.” The BJP leader’s remarks drew sharp criticism from Vijay’s party. TVK Minister Rajmohan condemned the statement and questioned whether Nagendran had maintained the dignity expected of a political leader. “It is a derogatory comment. He didn't speak as a leader; he spoke as if he were some street-corner speaker. It is not acceptable. We strongly condemn this. One should speak with respect and meaningfully. He should uphold the dignity of the position he holds,” Rajmohan said. Former state BJP president K Annamalai also criticised Nagendran’s remarks. Annamalai called the statement “highly condemnable” and said political disagreements should remain focused on policies, ideology and governance rather than the families of political opponents. “Those in politics must be responsible for their words and actions. Differences of opinion may exist. Policies can be critiqued. The functioning of the government can be questioned. However, speaking in a manner that insults someone’s family members, especially their mother, is utterly unacceptable in any way,” Annamalai said. Annamalai further criticised the tone of political discourse in Tamil Nadu. “Such low-quality remarks represent a politics that became obsolete thirty or forty years ago. items.title: Karnataka’s Beda Bro campaign targets Gen Z, but is the message getting through?
items.summary: We have never received an email about this particular campaign that has been going on by the government of Karnataka. So I was quite surprised.” Karan, a fourth-year Social Sciences major, is closely involved in substance-abuse awareness work on his campus, at a Bengaluru university that keeps close contact with Karnataka police on drug-related issues. Yet, when asked about the state government’s Beda Bro campaign, he said he had not heard of it. The campaign is a government initiative designed as a social message geared towards helping young people unapologetically say "No" to drugs. Spearheaded by Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Information Technology & Biotechnology, and e-Governance, it was launched alongside Operation RISE (Refuse, Inform, Support, Empower) on June 30, as part of its anti-drug efforts. Since its launch, the campaign has been rolled out through police events, college programmes, awareness activities, and partnerships with private institutions. In Dakshina Kannada , Mysuru , and Belagavi , district police and local officials have held briefings, college events, and documentary screenings combining enforcement, awareness, and counselling support. In Bengaluru, LuLu Mall Rajajinagar partnered with the Bengaluru City Police for a “Beda Bro, Say No to Drugs” rally on July 25, while a candle march was held with Kengeri police station and VV Group of Institutions. More events have been promoted through individual institutions' social media accounts. Karan is one of the eight Bengaluru college students we interviewed to know if a campaign designed to reach young people is reaching them, and what they think of its messaging. Most said they had not heard of Beda Bro before being contacted for this story. One had seen a video from the campaign on X, formerly Twitter. While this sample cannot establish how widely Beda Bro has reached young people across Karnataka, it raises a question about how the campaign is reaching its intended audience, particularly through the digital platforms and institutional channels young people already use. ‘I had no idea what the campaign is about’ Karan said his university regularly communicates drug-related information in coordination with the police, but he had not received any communication about Beda Bro specifically.
